name: International Protection (Refugee Status / Subsidiary Protection)

requirements.blocker_text: The Ministry of the Interior and Public Administration (International Protection Procedures Division, Migration Directorate) decides international-protection claims. Applicants express intent to any public authority as soon as possible after entry; police establish identity and entry route; the applicant is transferred to the Asylum Home (or its Logatec branch) for formal lodging, medical exam, photographing, and fingerprinting; a first interview on the merits follows (or a Dublin interview if another EU state is responsible). Recognized refugees (persecution on race, ethnic origin, religion, nationality, social group, or political opinion) receive a PERMANENT residence permit effective from the decision date. The regular procedure has a statutory 6-month first-instance deadline (frequently exceeded in practice; 6 months to 3 years is typical), while accelerated cases should decide within 2 months. There is no formal appeal, but an administrative dispute (judicial review) can be filed within 15 days (regular procedure) or 3 days (accelerated/other decisions), proceeding to the Administrative Court, then Supreme Court, then Constitutional Court.
requirements.fix_path: Express intent to apply for international protection to any public authority, then complete registration, formal lodging at the Asylum Home, and the merits interview.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicants who do not meet the refugee-status criteria but face serious harm -- death penalty, torture, or serious threats from armed conflict -- receive subsidiary protection: a TEMPORARY residence permit whose duration matches the assessed threat period, through the same procedure as refugee status.
requirements.fix_path: Complete the same international-protection application process; subsidiary protection is granted where refugee criteria are not met but serious-harm criteria are.

outcome.duration_length: indefinite (refugee status: immediate permanent residence); matches threat-assessment period (subsidiary protection: temporary residence)

sources.title: Portal GOV.SI (Government of the Republic of Slovenia) -- Ministry of the Interior's role, refugee status granting immediate permanent residence, subsidiary protection's temporary residence, application process

Asylum Information Database (AIDA, European Council on Refugees and Exiles) -- detailed procedural timelines: 6-month regular/2-month accelerated first-instance deadlines, 15-day/3-day judicial-review windows, court appeal chain

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Slovenia). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- the core hard requirements (refugee and subsidiary-protection criteria, deciding body, and the immediate-permanent-residence outcome for refugees) are sourced directly to gov.si, tier 1; the detailed procedural timelines are corroborated by AIDA/ECRE, a tier-3 specialist NGO source, not independently required to be tier 1 since they support rather than constitute the hard requirement itself. GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE, MARQUEE FINDING: recognized refugees in Slovenia receive a PERMANENT residence permit immediately upon the recognition decision -- not a renewable temporary status that later converts -- a notably strong outcome compared to most other countries' asylum files built in this dataset, where refugee status typically starts temporary. HONEST DISCLOSURE: the tier-3 source notes the statutory 6-month regular-procedure deadline is 'frequently not observed' in practice, with real-world waits of 6 months to 3 years -- a gap between law and practice worth flagging rather than only stating the formal rule. citizenship_after_months set 60 as an approximation given no source found a distinct accelerated citizenship timeline for refugees specifically (the general 10-year standard track in si_citizenship_naturalisation.json may or may not apply unmodified -- not confirmed either way, so this figure is a reasonable-default estimate, not a confirmed rule).
